A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PaperRegister study. All pages, including appendices, are readable, and the methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched across the revised layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments, component ablations, recognizer evaluations, PaSa integration results and latency measurements in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an indexing-time experiment in Table 5 and additional retrieval metrics in Appendix E.

M1.justification: v2 Section 4.4 introduces an optional faster indexing variant that directly extracts all node contents instead of performing extraction followed by bottom-up aggregation. The default hierarchical indexing, retrieval procedure, five schemas and recognizer training remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use LitSearch with 3,400 papers and 597 queries, and Flexible-grained Search with 4,200 papers and the same three granularity groups. v2 adds metrics and an indexing variant within this coverage; incomplete papers and niche domains are explicitly described as untested.

E2.justification: Table 4 removes Paragraphmax from the latency comparison, where v1 reported 4.2 seconds. It remains in the main retrieval comparison. The other comparator sets are retained; renaming Paper Splitting to Multi-field Indexing does not introduce new chunk or paragraph methods.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds Precision, MAP and NDCG at cutoffs 5 and 10. Table 5 introduces a controlled indexing comparison using indexing hours and average recall. The retained experiments report the same split sizes, model choices, chunk length and training budgets.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused ablation testing whether direct extraction can reduce offline indexing time at an acceptable retrieval-quality cost. The existing layer ablations, recognizer and reward analyses, and PaSa compatibility experiment are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 newly marks results significant against the best baseline at p < 0.05. The statistical test, repeated-run counts and seeds are unspecified, so this establishes added significance reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: Appendix E substantially expands results with precision, MAP and NDCG across the main comparisons, while Table 5 adds indexing-time and recall trade-offs. Table 1 changes DPR LitSearch Chunkavg R@5/R@10 from 58.1/67.6 to 49.7/58.6 and Chunkmax from 67.9/75.5 to 72.6/79.7 under the same stated settings. PaperRegister's main recall scores remain identical.

T1.justification: The hierarchical-node definitions, indexing and relevance equations, SFT loss, hierarchical reward and GRPO objective are mathematically unchanged. Numbering the GRPO objective as Equation 12 adds no theoretical content, and neither version adds proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim flexible-grained retrieval through hierarchical indexing, an accurate low-latency recognizer trained with hierarchical rewards, and state-of-the-art performance with larger advantages on finer queries. v2's contribution bullets restate these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning LLM dependence, computational and storage demands, and untested incomplete or niche-domain papers. It also interprets direct extraction as a practical accuracy-cost trade-off. v1 acknowledged limited corpus scale but lacked these specific qualifications and the offline-cost interpretation.

D1.justification: Table 5 newly discloses offline indexing times of 47.6 hours for PaperRegister and 14.5 hours for the direct-extraction variant. Conversely, v2 omits v1's statement about manually balancing training examples across views; this omission does not establish an actual sampling change. Core hardware, hyperparameters, prompts and code access information are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works are retained, but v2 explicitly connects the chunk and paragraph comparisons to Multi-Field Adaptive Retrieval by Li et al. (2025b). The baseline description and related-work discussion sharpen the distinction between flat multi-field indexing and PaperRegister's hierarchy.

P1.justification: v2 edits and shortens prose, adds contribution bullets, numbers sections, reorders the dataset-construction explanation and divides related work into named categories. Appendix headings become descriptive and the author/affiliation block expands. The main narrative sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises typography, figure sizing and placement, redraws Figures 1–2, and relocates the unchanged schema figures. Table 4 gains recall columns, Table 5 adds the indexing-cost display, and Tables 7–9 add extensive metric grids. Table 6 redisplays dataset counts already stated in v1.

improvement.justification: v1's efficiency discussion focused on online latency; v2 adds offline indexing costs and an explicit accuracy-cost trade-off, making practical applicability easier to assess. Additional ranking metrics and specific limitations also strengthen the paper. These gains are incremental: the significance-test procedure remains unspecified, while the balanced-sampling detail and Paragraphmax latency comparison are omitted.
